source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check basic information, ex: IC, version of Rev TPM ACPI table, TPM Device Interface, Hash Algorithm,......

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Check basic information, ex: IC, version of Rev TPM ACPI table, TPM Device Interface, Hash Algorithm,......

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ls -l /dev/tpm* /dev/tpmrm* 2>&1; echo ---; cat /sys/class/tpm/tpm0/tpm_version_major 2>&1; echo ---; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -i tpm | tail -10 2>&1"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return /dev/tpm* presence + tpm_version_major + the TPM dmesg lines (firmware rev, TPM ACPI table rev, device interface, hash algorithms) so the user confirms basic TPM info per spec.

original_test_intent: Collect and compare TPM identity/IC, firmware revision, TPM ACPI table revision, device interface, supported hash algorithms and other owner-required basic information using read-only interfaces.
original_method: The agent enumerates all TPM nodes and drivers, captures raw sysfs/kernel information, approved TPM fixed properties/algorithms and ACPI data, maps every requested field to its authoritative source and compares it with the project specification.
manual_activity: A user supplies the expected information schema, approved tools and target. No physical or visual core activity is required, and engineer verdict remains separate from the automated collection.
required_inputs: Required field list and expected values, including meaning of the ellipsis
Read-only privilege/credential scope and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Keep all commands read-only; do not clear, own, provision, self-test with writes, generate keys or modify NV state.
Enumerate devices instead of assuming tpm0 and bind every output to the correct TPM.
Preserve full raw output rather than only tailing ten log lines.
Stop on unknown side effects, ambiguous mapping or security-state anomaly; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect all approved device, sysfs, fixed-property, algorithm, ACPI, driver and firmware information.
Record exact tool versions and map each requested field to raw evidence.
Compare with expected values and report gaps/tool results without deciding PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Supply the complete field schema and expected values.
Approve any additional read-only package and access.
Review comparison and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Useful as a preliminary inventory, but fixed `/sys/class/tpm/tpm0`, dmesg tailing and claimed field coverage are not reliable across platforms.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the original command text as history, but enumerate all TPM nodes and use approved read-only TPM capability and ACPI tools where each requested field requires them.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All explicitly named fields, open-ended additional fields and the 5/20-minute values are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: EXPAND READ-ONLY COLLECTION TO MATCH THE REQUESTED SCHEMA
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a field-to-source table from enumerated device/sysfs data, TPM fixed properties/algorithms, kernel driver output and ACPI TPM table data, preserving full raw evidence.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Target OS/kernel and TPM implementation with owner-approved tools.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record OS/kernel, TPM firmware, tpm2-tools and ACPI-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner TPM/platform field specification; tool commands must be validated for installed versions.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes fixed-path/truncated-log assumptions and supplies fields from authoritative interfaces.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Improves completeness without adding state changes.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Field schema, expected values, identity and tool approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some vendor IC/revision fields may require an approved vendor read-only interface; absence must be reported, not fabricated.

project_override_considerations: Projects define which additional fields the ellipsis includes and their expected values. Missing expected data affects readiness/comparison, not automation capability or permanent blocked status.
expected_evidence: Expected field/value schema, platform/TPM identity, tool versions and authorization
Raw enumerated device/sysfs, fixed-property, algorithm, ACPI, driver and firmware outputs
Field-to-evidence mapping with unavailable/ambiguous items explicit
No-state-change verification, security/host health and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The open-ended field list is underspecified but internally consistent; project schema supplies completeness and expected values.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Missing field expectations or optional packages are readiness inputs. Read-only data collection remains fully automatable.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keep YES capability but reject claims that its short fixed-path command proves all fields.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain its evidence/tool improvements while reclassifying FULLY AUTOMATABLE under V3.1.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates package/schema confirmation and engineer verdict from core automated capability.

review_improvement: Provides auditable coverage for each requested TPM field instead of equating generic dmesg lines with ACPI, interface and algorithm evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Every requested datum is an electronic read from the OS/firmware interfaces; no physical or human observation is intrinsic. Expected values and optional tools govern readiness, so the case is fully automatable.
